newsitem.title: PERU: Peru pension companies see funds doubling by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Peru pension companies see funds doubling by 2000.

text.p: Peru's Association of Pension Funds predicted Tuesday their total portfolios would more than double to $3.148 billion in 2000 from the current level of $1.473 billion.

"That is an important growth which reflects the effective management of the pension associations and what they can give affiliated workers," Jaime Caceres, president of the Association of Pension Funds, told a news conference.
Peru's five private pension funds (AFPs) currently have 1.65 million contributors, or affiliates, and they expect to reach 1.80 million by the end of this year, the association said.

Since their 1993 outset, the funds have achieved an average annual 23.20 percent growth rate in nominal terms, and 9.2 percent in real terms. In the last 12 months, nominal growth was 25.17 percent and real growth 15.06 percent.
The funds invest 49.70 percent of money in the financial system, 35.01 percent in the Lima Stock Exchange, 14.86 percent in private businesses, and 0.44 percent with the Central Bank of Reserves.
